lists.name: Juno Awards: Album of the Year

podcast.body: Released in mid-1999, this album included the song "Bobcaygeon," which went on to become the Juno single of the year in 2000. "From the Phantom Power album of mid 1999 the Juno single of the year in 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The album "Phantom Power" contains the song "Escape is in Hand for the Traveling Man," which was inspired by Jim Ellison of Material Issue. This connection highlights the influence of Powerpop artists on other genres and bands. "If you're familiar with the tragically hip song, Escape is in hand for the Traveling Man, that's from their Phantom Power album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The song "Poets" from this 1998 album was recorded at their own studio, The Bath House, where the yellow aviation contraption featured on the album cover is actually kept on a shelf in one of the recording rooms. "This is from the Phantom Power album in 1998, and the yellow aviation contraption that we've seen on the cover is actually sitting on a shelf in one of the recording rooms."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album features the song "Fireworks," which contains lyrics referencing Paul Henderson's famous goal in the 1972 Canada-Russia Series. It also includes the song "Thompson Girl." "lines from the song Fireworks from the Phantom Power album that talks about Paul Henderson's famous goal."

podcast.body: This album features the song "Poets." "From the Phantom Power album of 1998, that's the tragically hit with poets featuring, of course, Gord Downey, the band's frontman and lyricist, and a poet himself."
